title: Stellar XDR corpus manifest
description: Draft 0.2. Index of corpus entries. Each entry is one XDR value in its own file, tagged with the CAP and protocol version that introduced or changed its shape, where it came from, and the values a correct decoder must report.

built_with.description: The XDR library and protocol version the corpus was last generated and verified with.

id.description: Stable identifier. Never reused, never renamed.

xdr_type.description: Name of the top-level XDR type in the file, as spelled in the .x definitions (for example LedgerCloseMeta, TransactionEnvelope, ScVal).

file.description: Path of the raw binary XDR file, relative to the manifest.

caps.description: CAPs that introduced or changed the shape this entry exercises.

introduced.description: First protocol version in which the network can emit this shape.

captured.description: Protocol version of the ledger or XDR definitions the entry was produced under.

synthetic.description: True when the entry was built by the generator rather than taken from a ledger closed by stellar-core.

shapes.description: Tags for the rare patterns the entry contains. Used for per-CAP coverage reports.

expect.description: What a correct decoder must report. Every decoder must also re-encode the value to the exact bytes in the file.

probe.description: Name of the probe a runner applies to the decoded value to extract the values below.

values.description: Expected decoded values. 64-bit integers are decimal strings so no JSON parser can round them.

may_refuse.description: Keys of values for which raising an explicit error is an accepted outcome, because the SDK's native representation cannot hold the value without loss. Returning a different value silently is never accepted.

build.description: Encode-side cases for SDK builders that take untyped input, such as an ID written as a string. A runner applies them only where its SDK has such a builder. At least one of `accept` and `refuse` is present.

probe.description: Name of the builder probe a runner feeds the inputs below to.

accept.description: Canonical inputs. The builder must encode exactly the value given in `encodes`.

refuse.description: Inputs that are not a canonical value in range. The builder must raise an error. Encoding any value from them is a wrong value.

sightings.description: Public issues or pull requests where this shape broke a decoder or indexer.

build_input.description: Named arguments for a builder probe. A string is passed as a string. {"float": "N"} is passed as the floating-point number N, for SDKs whose builders also take numbers.

generator.description: Name of the generator function that builds the entry deterministically.

network_passphrase.description: Passphrase used for signatures and hashes, when the entry has any.
